A random forest bootstraps training rows independently for each tree and samples candidate features again at every split. Sampling features once for the whole tree is not the usual random-forest algorithm. Aggregate class votes with a deterministic tie rule. The file includes the CART implementation so it runs independently. Out-of-bag evaluation and probabilistic averaging are useful extensions, not implemented here.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** If trees had equal variance $\sigma^2$ and pairwise correlation $\rho$, averaging $T$ predictions would give variance $\sigma^2[\rho+(1-\rho)/T]$. This illustrates why decorrelating trees through row/feature randomness matters: adding trees cannot remove a shared correlated error component. Classification vote behavior is not exactly this regression variance formula, but the intuition remains useful. [3](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/ensemble.html)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://mlcourse.ai/book/topic05/topic5_part2_random_forest.html) and [2](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/ensemble.html#forest).
